rows.description:
invideo editor trimmed two raw takes (54 seconds) into a 45.4-second first cut I can still edit.
Try invideo editor free: https://invideo.io/i/FutureAI

Client work is really two jobs, the edit and the revision rounds, and in Premiere Pro both of them land on me. This is my complete editing workflow for client talking-head work: raw takes in, a first cut back, and the changes handled on a timeline I still control. I gave the invideo editor agent instructions for the first cut in plain language and let it work through the footage. It trimmed the head and tail air, joined the intro straight into the outro, and normalized the dialogue to -16 LUFS with levels matched across the join. The first cut came back as an editable timeline, not a locked video. I reviewed it the way I would before a client round, marked what needed changing, then moved clips and adjusted sections myself so the storytelling and pacing were my call.

invideo editor is an agentic video editor: you give its AI agents the editing assignment in plain language, they carry it out on an editable timeline, and the timeline stays yours. invideo editor is free to use; the agents use credits when you hand them work. rows.title: How to Cut Montages with Video Editing Workflow AI (Step by Step)
rows.description:
invideo editor reviewed a folder of travel clips, built a base cut on an editable timeline, and laid my music track underneath, at 1920x1080, 24 fps.
Try invideo editor free: https://invideo.io/i/BusinessLens

I wanted to see how much of my video editing workflow AI could take over. Cutting a montage to music in Premiere usually means auditioning every shot, trimming to the beat by hand, and redoing it all when the track changes. Here's how I handed that first pass to invideo editor instead:

1. I loaded my travel clips into the media pool in invideo editor, right in the browser (projects handle up to 200 GB of footage).
2. I asked the agent in plain language to review the videos and add the usable ones to the timeline.
3. It came back with a base cut: individual clips in a shot order on the video track, not a flattened render.
4. The agent added the music layer underneath, and I played it back to judge the pacing.
5. I handed the project off to Premiere Pro, where it arrived as separate clips on multiple tracks, so I could make the final calls myself.

That's the part of my video editing workflow AI should handle. invideo editor is an agentic video editor: its agents do the editing you describe in plain language, on an editable timeline that stays yours. rows.title: How to Use AI to Speed Up Your Video Editing Workflow
rows.description:
I walk through how I use AI to speed up my editing workflow.
I'll cover all the AI tools I use in VEED. https://veed.io/

I’ve been editing for over 20 years, and AI tools now save me hours every week. In this video, I show how I use VEED to move faster with subtitles, clean audio, background removal, image generation, voiceovers, and eye contact correction.

First, I use AI subtitles. I click auto subtitle, and in seconds my video has clean, styled captions. This helps when people watch with the sound off and it saves me from hiring someone to do it.

Next, I use AI clean audio. I turn it on, and it removes background noise for me. I don’t need to mess with audio settings. It just fixes the sound fast.

I also use the AI background remover. What used to take a long time now takes a few clicks. I can remove the background and add a new one right inside my editor.

When I need B-roll, I use AI image generation. I type what I want, and it creates it for me. I can also generate an AI voice over by pasting in a script and picking a voice.

One more tool I like is AI eye contact. If I’m looking off screen, it adjusts my eyes so it looks like I’m looking at the camera.

These AI tools help me edit videos faster and keep my editing workflow simple every day.
